title: One methodology, one buildable sport: NBA's market is near-perfectly calibrated
headline_insight: Under a single shared reliability methodology, only NBA's market map clears the honesty floor -- and there the market's in-game ECE is 0.0064 across 1593 games.
what_it_means: The same three-part check (calibration, favorite-vs-longshot bias, comeback rate) is run per sport. NBA passes: market ECE 0.0064, and favorites at 0.60-plus win 0.8997 of the time against a 0.8948 implied price, a gap of just +0.005. MLB, soccer and tennis lacked buckets meeting the n>=30 floor, so they are marked not_buildable rather than guessed.
how_to_read: The table has one row per sport; a status of ok carries the metrics, while not_buildable carries the reason it could not be computed.
why_it_matters: It shows the methodology is portable and the honesty floor is real -- three of four sports do not clear it and say so outright.
caveat: This is a single-sport result today (NBA only); MLB, soccer and tennis are not_buildable, and tennis has no reliability map at all.
